title: fix: enable FaceTime HD cameras on Intel Macs
head: 92ef77156ca4
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A chatty lspci response silently completes the camera migration without touching the camera
leads.consequence: With 14e4:1570 early in lspci output and more output after it, grep -q exits early, lspci receives SIGPIPE, and pipefail makes the negated condition true. The migration exits zero, the migration runner stamps its per-user completion marker, installs no packages, and subsequent updates will not retry even if lspci subsequently works. The newly added test uses just one lspci line, missing this case. Use grep without -q, redirect its output, and distinguish a failed producer from a negative match.
leads.triage: corroborated; = Opus N2 (lspci pipefail); published in More findings

leads.summary: The proposed repository's FaceTime DKMS source is too old for the currently packaged kernel
leads.consequence: The dependency PR pins patjak/facetimehd 0.7.0.2, whose fthd_v4l2.c:399 unconditionally calls strncpy. The packaged linux-omarchy is 7.2.5, and Linux 7.2 headers/fortify no longer provide that function; upstream facetimehd fixed this in commit 54fb8f2, which the pinned 0.7.0.2 predates. DKMS cannot build the camera module on that kernel. The dependency's post-transaction verifier intentionally tests pkgbase == linux only, not linux-omarchy or linux-t2, so its own verifier cannot catch that missing module. No DKMS compile was executed here; the source incompatibility is direct but package transaction behavior should be confirmed with a sandbox/physical machine.
leads.triage: corroborated; = Opus N3b (0.7.0.2 strncpy vs 7.2); published

leads.summary: Package availability is a hard release prerequisite, but the recipes are still in an open dependency PR
leads.consequence: omarchy-pkgs#182 remains OPEN, and both recipes are absent from its base source tree. If the selected live ISO or installed-system repository lacks either package when the PR ships, omarchy-iso/builder/build-iso.sh passes both names to pacman -Syw and aborts; merely listing them cannot package them. Existing-install migrations similarly fail omarchy-pkg-add's pacman -S lookup and remain pending. Release/order dependency: verify the exact binary repositories for each supported channel and publish working packages before building/shipping this PR; do not remove the list entries. The actual binary repository index was not fetched, so current binary availability is unverified.

leads.summary: Three open camera PRs independently add the same leaf; two add a second migration and duplicate offline entries
leads.consequence: Open, divergent PRs #11381, #12067 and #12686 all create this leaf with incompatible install commands and independent migration IDs. Merging either #12067 or #12686 without reconciliation produces two copies each of facetimehd-dkms and facetimehd-firmware in the ISO package list and two migrations that repeat the installation on the same device. #11381's competing migration uses a different AUR delivery. An actual three-way file merge against each other's merge base produces conflicts in both the leaf and test for #12067/#12686, and the leaf for #11381. Decide which implementation is kept and retire/dedupe other migrations, not just resolve markers; GH reports each other's mergeable state against quattro as MERGEABLE, not this pairwise combination.
leads.triage: confirmed_by_coordinator; gh api files of #11381, #12067, #12686; Opus draft check refined; published as N5

leads.summary: The optional per-sensor calibration package is omitted from both install paths and ISO mirror
leads.consequence: The driver searches for nine sensor-specific set files and explicitly proceeds without calibration if the matching file is missing; both proposed packages include only the common firmware and driver. The separate facetimehd-data recipe proposed in omarchy-pkgs#556 supplies four of these files (9112, 1771, 1871, 1874), including the Apple MacBookAir 0x9770 case. Until that package is available and installed, those camera sensors boot without their supported calibration; the effect on an actual video feed was not measured. If complete hardware support is intended, package and list facetimehd-data (and evaluate sources for the remaining five sensor files).
leads.triage: confirmed_by_opus_followup; followup-561fa7ab.md 3b; published as optional note O3

leads.summary: New test gives no coverage for a failed or unregistered package transaction
leads.consequence: The test shadows the real omarchy-pkg-add twice with stubs that always succeed, and the second one marks packages installed without checking either requested name. A regression where a missing package is never registered, where pacman -S fails, or where a package is not in the configured repo is invisible. The test's 'installs firmware' and retry messages only verify a logged helper invocation and simulated successful marker; add a failure case plus a mock respecting per-package pacman -Q / -S and check nonzero installer or migration exit and retry behavior.
leads.triage: merged; overlaps F5/O1; stub fidelity not published separately

leads.summary: An unconditional Limine rebuild blocks the repair on non-Limine or broken-UKI installs
leads.consequence: This migration changes /etc/modules-load.d, which systemd reads in userspace at each boot; it does not change a mkinitcpio MODULES/HOOKS drop-in. Nevertheless `sudo limine-mkinitcpio` is unconditional. A user with an alternate boot setup without this binary (or an unrelated failing Limine rebuild) gets a failed migration, no machine or per-user marker, and `omarchy update` stops at this step after packages and config have already been written. Existing optional rebuild migrations guard `omarchy-cmd-present limine-mkinitcpio`. Standard ISO installs use Limine; confirm whether non-Limine/manual installs are supported before assigning broader severity.
leads.triage: confirmed_by_opus_followup; followup-561fa7ab.md 3a: binary present on all relevant installs, rebuild redundant; failure blocks queue; published as N4 with self-check correction

leads.summary: Mac support manual omits the newly claimed automatic FaceTime fix
leads.consequence: The manual's explicit list of installer-applied Mac hardware fixes names Broadcom Wi-Fi, SPI keyboard and NVMe suspend but not the new FaceTime camera step. The related open PRs #12067 and #12686 update this exact sentence. Add this hardware fix to the list after it is operational.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** a failed driver build still completes the migration; packages are unpublished.

[Earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13192#issuecomment-5838582465): AUR, headers, migration, tests **resolved**; failed-build success, `bdc_pci` **still present**.

### Still present: a failed build completes the migration

Arch's dkms hook returns 0 on a failed build, so the migration still writes its marker; later runs skip. The pinned 0.7.0.2 driver uses `strncpy()`, gone in Linux 7.2.

**Suggested change:** fail without the marker if DKMS did not build `facetimehd` for the boot kernel.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 92ef771)</summary>

# Reproducer: a facetimehd module that was never built still marks migration 1790297558 complete

Reviewed commit: `92ef77156ca43b6f0596c1116483a14d9250512b` (PR head at 2026-10-01T02:52Z). Its production files are identical to `561fa7ab`. Earlier results at `561fa7ab`, `d69d7e71` and `e75f42eb` are kept under "History" below.

Scenario: `facetimehd-dkms` installs, but its DKMS build fails. Arch's dkms ALPM hook (`/usr/share/libalpm/scripts/dkms`) prints a warning when `dkms install` fails and still returns 0, so `pacman -S`, and with it `omarchy-pkg-add`, succeed. The test stubs that outcome:

- package install succeeds
- `modprobe facetimehd` and `modinfo facetimehd` fail
- `dkms status` lists the module only as "added"
- `lsmod` lists no `bdc_pci`: no supported kernel builds that module, which was removed in Linux 5.12

The test asserts that the migration does not write its machine-wide completion marker in that state.

Run: save the file below as `test/shell.d/facetimehd-migration-load-failure-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR, then run `bash test/shell.d/facetimehd-migration-load-failure-test.sh`. Every command that would touch the system is stubbed, and the marker and config paths are redirected into a temporary directory.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

migration="$ROOT/migrations/1790297558.sh"

test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

stub_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
calls="$test_tmp/calls.log"
marker="$test_tmp/migration-complete"
mkdir -p "$stub_bin"
: >"$calls"

cat >"$stub_bin/lspci" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' '02:00.0 Multimedia controller [0480]: Broadcom Inc. and subsidiaries 720p FaceTime HD Camera [14e4:1570]'
SH
# The DKMS build of facetimehd failed. Arch's dkms ALPM hook prints a warning
# and still returns 0, so pacman, and with it omarchy-pkg-add, succeed.
cat >"$stub_bin/omarchy-pkg-add" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'omarchy-pkg-add\t%s\n' "$*" >>"$TEST_LOG"
SH
cat >"$stub_bin/limine-mkinitcpio" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'limine-mkinitcpio\n' >>"$TEST_LOG"
SH
# No facetimehd.ko exists for any kernel: loading it fails, and so does
# looking it up. DKMS still lists the source as added but not installed.
cat >"$stub_bin/modprobe" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'modprobe\t%s\n' "$*" >>"$TEST_LOG"
if [[ $1 == facetimehd ]]; then
  echo "modprobe: FATAL: Module facetimehd not found." >&2
  exit 1
fi
SH
cat >"$stub_bin/modinfo" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
echo "modinfo: ERROR: Module facetimehd not found." >&2
exit 1
SH
cat >"$stub_bin/dkms" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
[[ $1 == status ]] && echo "facetimehd/0.7.0.2: added"
exit 0
SH
cat >"$stub_bin/lsmod" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
echo "Module                  Size  Used by"
SH
cat >"$stub_bin/omarchy-state" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'omarchy-state\t%s\n' "$*" >>"$TEST_LOG"
SH
cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
if [[ $1 == tee ]]; then
  cat >"${@: -1}"
else
  "$@"
fi
SH
chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*

run_migration() {
  TEST_LOG="$calls" \
  OMARCHY_FACETIMEHD_MODULES_CONF="$test_tmp/modules-load-facetimehd.conf" \
  OMARCHY_FACETIMEHD_MODPROBE_CONF="$test_tmp/modprobe-facetimehd.conf" \
  OMARCHY_FACETIMEHD_MIGRATION_MARKER="$marker" \
  PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" \
  bash -euo pipefail "$migration"
}

status=0
run_migration >"$test_tmp/out" 2>&1 || status=$?

grep -Fxq $'modprobe\tfacetimehd' "$calls" ||
  fail "the migration tries to load facetimehd" "$(cat "$calls")"
pass "the migration tries to load facetimehd"

if (( status == 0 )) && [[ -e $marker ]]; then
  first_run=$(cat "$calls")
  : >"$calls"
  run_migration >/dev/null 2>&1
  fail "a facetimehd module that was never built does not mark the migration complete" \
    "first run exit status: $status, machine-wide marker written
first run output:
$(cat "$test_tmp/out")
first run commands:
$first_run
commands on the next run: $(wc -l <"$calls")"
fi
pass "a facetimehd module that was never built does not mark the migration complete"
```

Actual output at `92ef7715` (exit status 1; identical to `561fa7ab`, and the same on `92ef7715` merged into `quattro` `8b4eae66`). The migration says the module will load after a reboot, exits 0, requests a reboot and writes the machine-wide marker, so later runs for any user skip it. After the reboot there is still no module to load.

```text
ok - the migration tries to load facetimehd
first run exit status: 0, machine-wide marker written
first run output:
Installing FaceTime HD camera support
Could not load facetimehd now; it is configured to load after reboot.
first run commands:
omarchy-pkg-add	facetimehd-dkms facetimehd-firmware
limine-mkinitcpio
modprobe	facetimehd
omarchy-state	set reboot-required
commands on the next run: 0
not ok - a facetimehd module that was never built does not mark the migration complete
```

The PR's own test now asserts this behaviour for any load failure. Lines 199-210 of `test/shell.d/facetimehd-test.sh` at `92ef7715` ("a deferred module load records migration completion") expect exit 0, the "configured to load after reboot" message, the marker and reboot-required. Two changes compared:

1. Stopping on every load failure makes this test pass, but now fails the PR's test at "a facetimehd load failure is deferred without failing migration":

```diff
 elif ! sudo modprobe facetimehd 2>/dev/null; then
-  echo "Could not load facetimehd now; it is configured to load after reboot." >&2
+  echo "facetimehd did not load; check the DKMS build output above." >&2
+  exit 1
 fi
```

2. Stopping only when no module exists, and keeping the reboot fallback otherwise, makes this test pass:

```diff
 elif ! sudo modprobe facetimehd 2>/dev/null; then
+  if ! modinfo facetimehd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "facetimehd was not built; check the DKMS build output above." >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
   echo "Could not load facetimehd now; it is configured to load after reboot." >&2
 fi
```

   It also passes the PR's test, once that test gets a `modinfo` stub reporting the module as built, so the fallback case models "built but not loadable now":

```diff
 printf 'Module Size Used by\nbdc_pci 16384 0\n'
 SH
+cat >"$stub_bin/modinfo" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+exit 0
+SH
```

Actual output of this test with change 2 (exit status 0):

```text
ok - the migration tries to load facetimehd
ok - a facetimehd module that was never built does not mark the migration complete
```

Change 2 is an illustration. `modinfo` without `-k` checks the running kernel, so after a pending kernel update it could stop the migration until the reboot, which a retry then fixes. Checking `dkms status` for the kernel that will boot is the more precise test.

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

**New: `lspci -nn | grep -q` can skip the migration on the hardware it targets.** Under `omarchy-migrate`'s `pipefail`, `grep -q` can exit before `lspci` finishes writing, so the pipeline fails with 141 and `!` reads that as "no camera". The migration exits 0 and is recorded as done. Migration `1786137597` exists because `1785944594` failed this way. Reproduced with a deterministic stub; how often real output is long enough was not measured. **Suggested change:** use `grep '14e4:1570' >/dev/null`, as `1785944594` now does.

**New: the explicit `sudo limine-mkinitcpio` is not needed and can block the queue.** The package transaction already runs Limine's mkinitcpio hook, `facetimehd` loads from the root filesystem rather than the initramfs, and the only new image content is the `bdc_pci` blacklist. If the rebuild exits non-zero (for example when no FAT32 ESP is mounted, or a boot hook fails), the migration stops before its marker and blocks later migrations (source reading; not reproduced). **Suggested change:** drop the step, or at least keep its failure from stopping the migration (a presence check like `1786605598`'s is not enough).

**Still present: the `bdc_pci` handling targets a module no supported kernel has.** `bdc_pci` was removed in Linux 5.12 (`7766cafea0ec`), and `linux-omarchy` builds only the device-tree `USB_BDC_UDC` driver. The `blacklist bdc_pci` file, the `lsmod`-guarded unload and its "Could not unload" branch have no effect (source reading; not reproduced). **Suggested change:** remove them.

**New: overlapping open PRs.** #11381, #12067 and #12686 also add `install/hardware/apple/fix-facetimehd.sh` and a FaceTime migration; #12067 and #12686 also add both package names to `install/omarchy-other.packages`. Each adds the same new leaf path, so merging more than one conflicts. #11381 would also install AUR `facetimehd-dkms-git`, which conflicts with `facetimehd-dkms`. **Suggested change:** reconcile with those PRs so one leaf and one migration remain.

**New: possible conflict with AUR `facetimehd-dkms-git` (hypothesis, not run).** It provides and conflicts with `facetimehd-dkms`. `pacman -Q` does not resolve provides, and `--noconfirm` answers the conflict prompt with No, so the migration would fail on every update for those owners. **Suggested change:** skip the install when `pacman -T facetimehd-dkms facetimehd-firmware` succeeds.

- The migration test's `lsmod` stub always lists `bdc_pci`, so the path every supported kernel takes (no `bdc_pci`, direct load) is untested. A mutant that loads `facetimehd` only after unloading `bdc_pci` passes all 9 checks. A case whose `lsmod` lists no `bdc_pci` catches that mutant. The test's fallback case also asserts that a load failure writes the marker.
- `manual/44-mac-support.md` lists the Mac fixes the installer applies; adding the camera there would tell owners it is now set up.

# Reproducer: `lspci -nn | grep -q` under pipefail can skip migration 1790297558 on the hardware it targets

Reviewed commit: `92ef77156ca43b6f0596c1116483a14d9250512b` (PR head at 2026-10-01T02:52Z). Line 4 of the migration has not changed since `e75f42eb`. Earlier results are kept under "History" below.

`omarchy-migrate` runs each migration with `bash -euo pipefail`. The migration's hardware check is `if ! lspci -nn | grep -q '14e4:1570'; then exit 0; fi`, and it fails like this:

1. `grep -q` exits at the first match.
2. If `lspci` is still writing, it is killed by SIGPIPE (status 141).
3. pipefail makes the pipeline fail, and `!` turns that into "no camera".
4. The migration exits 0, and `omarchy-migrate` records it as done for that user.

Migration `1786137597` exists because migration `1785944594`'s T2 check failed this way on T2 Macs.

The `lspci` stub below keeps writing after the camera line, which makes the race deterministic. Whether a real Mac's `lspci -nn` output is long enough to trigger it was not measured.

Run: save the file below as `test/shell.d/facetimehd-migration-pci-check-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR, then run `bash test/shell.d/facetimehd-migration-pci-check-test.sh`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

migration="$ROOT/migrations/1790297558.sh"

test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT

stub_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
calls="$test_tmp/calls.log"
mkdir -p "$stub_bin"
: >"$calls"

# lspci is still writing when grep -q exits at the camera line, as with the
# T2 check that migration 1786137597 had to re-run. The long tail makes that
# deterministic here.
cat >"$stub_bin/lspci" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' '00:00.0 Host bridge [0600]: Intel Corporation Haswell-ULT DRAM Controller [8086:0a04]'
printf '%s\n' '02:00.0 Multimedia controller [0480]: Broadcom Inc. and subsidiaries 720p FaceTime HD Camera [14e4:1570]'
for ((i = 0; i < 20000; i++)); do
  printf '%s\n' '03:00.0 Network controller [0280]: Broadcom Inc. and subsidiaries BCM4360 802.11ac Wireless Network Adapter [14e4:43a0]'
done
SH
for command in omarchy-pkg-add limine-mkinitcpio modprobe omarchy-state; do
  cat >"$stub_bin/$command" <<SH
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\t%s\n' $command "\$*" >>"\$TEST_LOG"
SH
done
cat >"$stub_bin/lsmod" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
echo "Module                  Size  Used by"
SH
cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
if [[ $1 == tee ]]; then
  cat >"${@: -1}"
else
  "$@"
fi
SH
chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*

status=0
TEST_LOG="$calls" \
OMARCHY_FACETIMEHD_MODULES_CONF="$test_tmp/modules-load-facetimehd.conf" \
OMARCHY_FACETIMEHD_MODPROBE_CONF="$test_tmp/modprobe-facetimehd.conf" \
OMARCHY_FACETIMEHD_MIGRATION_MARKER="$test_tmp/migration-complete" \
PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" \
  bash -euo pipefail "$migration" >"$test_tmp/out" 2>&1 || status=$?

grep -Fq $'omarchy-pkg-add\tfacetimehd-dkms facetimehd-firmware' "$calls" ||
  fail "a Mac with the camera gets camera support even when lspci outlives grep" \
    "migration exit status: $status
migration output: $(cat "$test_tmp/out")
commands run: $(wc -l <"$calls")"
pass "a Mac with the camera gets camera support even when lspci outlives grep"
```

## What remains

Every migration scenario in the test uses one `lsmod` stub that lists `bdc_pci` (lines 90-93). The path every supported kernel takes, with `bdc_pci` absent so the migration goes straight to `modprobe facetimehd`, is never run. The mutation below makes the migration load `facetimehd` only after it has found and unloaded `bdc_pci`. On a kernel without `bdc_pci`, the mutated migration would print "Could not unload bdc_pci now" and never load the camera driver. The PR's test still passes:

   echo "Could not unload bdc_pci now; facetimehd is configured to load after reboot." >&2
